name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Ciliary Mesh Frond
description:
The Ciliary Mesh Frond is a bio-synthetic mesh network node grown from Zheng-Dao's proprietary piezoelectric cilia substrate — a branching, fern-like structure roughly the size of a hand that adheres to most surfaces and begins passively harvesting micro-vibrations within minutes of deployment. These harvested vibrations are converted into carrier energy that powers a low-footprint, frequency-hopping mesh relay, capable of extending an encrypted network node into areas with no existing infrastructure. The Frond is literally alive in a limited sense: its cilia respond to environmental stimuli, adjusting their resonance frequency to optimize signal routing without active user input.

The device's distinctive property is its near-zero RF emission profile during idle states. Rather than broadcasting continuously, the Frond listens and responds — it activates only when a paired handshake signal passes within range, acting as a silent repeater that leaves almost no trace on passive spectrum scans. Its biological substrate also means it registers as organic matter on most bio-scanners, not electronics, which allows it to pass through checkpoints concealed in plant material, food packaging, or even worn against skin under loose clothing.

Zheng-Dao markets the Frond to corporate field teams for infrastructure-denied environments, but its properties have made it equally popular among resistance cells and insurgent networks in GLMZ's outer districts. The irony that a Zheng-Dao product underpins much of the anti-corporate mesh in the city's peripheral zones is not lost on anyone — least of all Zheng-Dao's internal security division, which has reportedly been trying to introduce a remote-kill pathway into newer production runs.

specifications.relay_range: Up to 200m per node in open conditions; reduced in dense construction
specifications.network_capacity: Supports up to 12 simultaneous paired devices
specifications.power_source: Self-sustaining via ambient vibration harvesting; supplemental micro-cell extends range by 40%
specifications.activation_latency: 80–120ms from handshake signal to relay-active state
specifications.form_factor: Branching frond structure, ~22cm at full extension; collapsible to 8cm for transport
specifications.scanner_profile: Registers as organic matter on standard bio-scans; requires specialized EM analysis to identify

tactical_use: Deployed in advance of an operation to extend mesh network coverage into infrastructure-denied zones — abandoned sectors, corporate-locked districts, or areas under signal suppression. A single operative can seed a relay chain by placing Fronds along a route, creating an ephemeral private network that dissolves when the substrate is retrieved or degrades. Useful for coordinating multi-team operations without touching public or corporate communication infrastructure.
cultural_context: The Frond has acquired a quiet symbolic weight in GLMZ's outer districts, where residents have built permanent informal mesh networks from illegally obtained units. Finding a Frond adhered to a wall or ceiling in a squat or underground meeting space signals that the space is connected — part of the city's shadow infrastructure. Some community organizers have begun cultivating them openly as a statement, daring corporate security to arrest someone for growing a plant.
known_users: Community mesh stewards in the peripheral zones
Smugglers coordinating in signal-dead warehouse districts
story_hooks: A player discovers a Frond network in a supposedly abandoned sector — it's active, maintained, and routing traffic for someone who shouldn't be there.

Zheng-Dao reaches out through back channels: they want the players to recover a specific Frond from a resistance cache before a security audit team finds it and traces the network back to a Zheng-Dao employee who's been helping the resistance.
A new production run of Fronds has hit the black market, but three separate mesh networks built on them have gone silent simultaneously — something in the update is wrong.
A Frond has been growing on the exterior wall of a corporate checkpoint for eight months without anyone noticing; it's been logging every encrypted handshake that passes through.
